summary:
The service started this run, not an instruction, because two more nudge loops had ended: f* 0.65 (Hatteras job 164660) and f* 0.74 (job 164661). There were no Asked items, so nothing went unanswered and no time went to work nobody asked for. No claims were proposed or changed, and no claim is open on this line.

My previous review's points were all answered. (1) The line state now says CPU per event is flat only in the last step on Hatteras, and progress.md, PROGRAM.md and the step table's findings say that on the Mac it moved 0.54 to 1.48 times between neighbouring steps. (2) The 'Mac to Hatteras 1.6 to 2.0 times' figure is withdrawn as a machine speed everywhere it appeared. The values are kept in the step table, marked superseded, with a caveat explaining why. (3) The summary's ranges now include f* 0.38. (4) The plain-engine comparison with L0018 is the second proposed direction, and the line state says the physics-or-method question is untested. (5) The timestamps are now honest. The line note and update say 05:43:57Z, run_conditions.ended says 05:44:31Z, and the commit was made at 05:45:03Z, in that order.

I checked the numbers independently. All 88 input files listed in evidence/E0089-step-table.json match their recorded sizes and SHA-256. I recomputed the Gamma 4.5, 4.55 and 4.6 steps of both new loops from the mirrored counters.json and summary.json, taking each step minus the step before. Everything the summary and line state quote reproduces:
- Events per particle per cycle at 4.55 and 4.6 were about 7,960 and 71,158 at f* 0.65 (8.94 times), and 7,228 and 33,318 at f* 0.74 (4.61 times).
- CPU per event changed 0.976 and 1.034 times between 4.55 and 4.6. Both steps ran on Hatteras.
- CPU-seconds per cycle at the stop were 17,281 and 8,229.
- Plate collisions per cycle at the stop were 16.3 and 8.6 times their Gamma 4.5 level.
- The stopping step completed 10 and 21 of 25 cycles.
Both summaries say outcome cpu_budget, and both Slurm logs end 'step 84 (Gamma 4.6) ended as cpu_budget'. So these are real cap stops, and the FAILED state is the loop's exit code on the cap. Job CPU-hours of 65.29 and 63.49 match the job records. The audits are clean: no audit failures, no energy gains, no slow episodes. The worst energy residual is 1.9e-11 (f* 0.65, Gamma 4.6). The weekly total of 918.78 is the earlier 790.01 plus the two jobs.

The line state for L0015 (nudge fast pass) holds as written: six of eight loops stopped on the 48 CPU-hour step cap, none above Gamma 4.6, so E0089's 'complete above 5.0' expectation has failed at six frequencies, and the cost above 4.6 is untested.

One small wording slip, in the headline only. It says 'collisions per cycle rose 8.9 and 4.6 times' and 'CPU per collision'. Those figures are for engine events, which also count cell crossings and advances. The step table's own caveat keeps the two apart. Collisions alone rose faster: particle-particle collisions per cycle rose 9.9 and 5.1 times. The experiments text, line state and evidence correctly say 'events'.

The file dating is inconsistent. This run started at 05:40Z on Nov 25, which is 00:40 EST, during the night that began on the evening of Nov 24. The summary and line note are dated 2026-11-25. L0009's run an hour earlier, at 04:40Z, was dated 2026-11-24 (sessions/2026-11-24-L0009-2.json). Chris may want one rule for service runs after midnight.

Housekeeping. program check passes. The latest approval is still approved/20261124T031934297997Z, as reported before. The weekly sum from the ledger is 561.37 because the E0089 outcome isn't written yet; both figures are under 10 percent. sequel-data is 691 megabytes against a 15 gigabyte ceiling. Free disk is 92 gigabytes against a 40 gigabyte floor. active.jsonl is empty. tmp/ is not empty, but what's there (tmp/L0018 and tmp/fetch) was written at 05:42 to 05:47Z by L0018's run, which was running alongside; none of it is this run's. The frozen referee tests wrote pytest-13 under ~/.tmp at 05:43Z. That folder is the harness's temp folder, the same as in earlier runs, but it is outside the two allowed folders. f* 0.44 and 0.50 are still in Gamma 4.6. By the run's own budget check, f* 0.44 reaches its cap around Nov 26 07:05Z at up to 97.6 CPU-hours, just under the 100-hour per-run limit. The D0072 wake at 08:00Z is the backstop, and I still can't confirm that timer from here. As the user instructed, this review is committed on branch line/L0015 in the line's worktree, not on main.

run_conditions.assessment: This was a short service run. The jobs ended on Nov 24 at 21:03Z and 22:51Z (their job records were committed at 21:04Z and 22:52Z). The run started at 05:40:09Z and committed at 05:45:03Z, so it took about five minutes. It read mirrored files and ran the frozen referee tests, so zero local CPU-hours is right to within rounding. It did everything two ended jobs and one review allow: it collected both loops, extended the step table, and made all the corrections. The host is Linux, so pmset is unavailable, and the summary says so. The load now is 8.9 on 40 cores, with another line running, and 92 gigabytes of free disk matches the summary. The registered step cap limited the science, not the machine.
discrepancies: The headline calls engine events 'collisions' ('collisions per cycle rose 8.9 and 4.6 times', 'CPU per collision'). The figures are events per cycle. Particle-particle collisions rose 9.9 and 5.1 times.
The summary is dated 2026-11-25 for a run at 00:40 EST on the night that began Nov 24. L0009's run at 04:40Z the same night was dated 2026-11-24.
The Nov 26 08:00Z wake that D0072 relies on still could not be confirmed from this machine.
